rendered:
The question's premise does not hold. The document does not report NFA-F as having the best capacity retention after cycling. It reports the reverse. In the retention curves of Fig. 8[1], NFA-F ends lowest of the NFA variants. The text says the NFA-A variant maintained ≈80% capacity after 100 cycles when compared with the NFA 811 (≈70%) and NFA-F[2] The NFA-F value is given as ≈50%[3]. NFA-A is described as the most stable, with the highest retention reported for the NFA variants: superior capacity retention (≈80%)[4].

The document gives only a partial explanation for NFA-F's weaker behaviour. It notes that NFA-F has the lowest aluminium content of the variants, (LiNi0.8Fe0.15Al0.05O2, 5% Al)[5], while the other variants have variants with 15% and 10% aluminum in their compositions[6]. It states that the NFA-A variant was the most stable in the test conditions when compared with the other variants: was the most stable in these test conditions when compared[7]. It does not give a specific mechanism for the faster fade of NFA-F in the retention test.
